title: Word Break
interviewTips: Clarify reuse: ask if dictionary words can be reused unlimited times (yes) and if empty string / empty wordDict are possible.
Trade-off to discuss: brute-force DFS enumerates all partitions O(2^n) vs DP memoizes reachable prefixes O(n*L); mention Trie optimization when wordDict is large.
Edge-case tip: mention worst case s='aaaa...b' with wordDict=['a','aa','aaa'] causing exponential blowup without memo/DP, and check max word length pruning.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force
approaches.intuition: Try every possible split position. Starting at index i, try every end j>i where s[i:j] is a dictionary word, then recursively solve suffix starting at j. If any path reaches end of string, answer is true.
approaches.theory: This is exhaustive DFS over the partition tree. Root is index 0, children of i are all j>i with s[i:j] in wordSet. Search succeeds if node n is reachable. Correct because any valid segmentation corresponds to a root-to-leaf path. Without memoization subproblems (same suffix index) are recomputed many times, leading to exponential time.

timeComplexity.explanation: In worst case each index branches into n-i choices. Number of partitions of length-n string is 2^(n-1). Each substring hash lookup is O(1) average, substring creation O(n). TLEs on cases like aaaa... with overlapping dict.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion depth up to n plus O(M) for hash set where M is total characters in wordDict. Substring copies add temporary O(n) cost.

steps: dfs(0): try j=1..8, s[0:4]='leet' in set -> call dfs(4)
dfs(4): try j=5..8, s[4:8]='code' in set -> call dfs(8)
dfs(8)==n -> return True, unwinds to True

edgeCases: s='a', wordDict=['a'] -> true; s='a', wordDict=['b'] -> false
Overlapping: s='aaaaaaa', wordDict=['aaa','aaaa'] -> true via 3+4, brute force explores many dead ends
Impossible suffix: s='aaaaab', wordDict=['a','aa','aaa'] -> false, explores full tree

approaches.name: Approach 2: Optimal Bottom-Up DP with Max-Length Pruning
approaches.intuition: Instead of re-solving suffixes, record which prefixes are breakable. dp[i]=true if s[0:i] can be segmented. To compute dp[i], look back at most maxLen characters: if dp[i-l] is true and s[i-l:i] is a word, then dp[i] is true.
approaches.theory: Optimal substructure: prefix i is breakable iff it extends a breakable prefix j with a dictionary word s[j:i]. This is forward reachability DAG where edges j->i exist if s[j:i] in dict. Processing i in increasing order guarantees dp[j] is final when used. Limiting lookback to maxLen = max word length preserves correctness and cuts O(n^2) to O(n*maxLen). dp[n] is answer.

timeComplexity.explanation: n = len(s), L = max word length. For each of n positions we check at most L substrings with O(1) hash lookup. Worst case O(n^2) when L ~ n, but typically much faster. Substring hashing cost bounded by L.

spaceComplexity.explanation: dp array O(n) plus hash set O(M) where M is total characters in wordDict.

steps: i=4: l=4, dp[0]=true and s[0:4]='leet' in set -> dp[4]=true
i=1,2,3,5,6,7 remain false (no word matches from a true prefix)
i=8: l=4, dp[4]=true and s[4:8]='code' in set -> dp[8]=true

edgeCases: s='applepenapple', wordDict=['apple','pen'] -> true with reuse of 'apple'
s='', wordDict=[] -> true (empty prefix); s='a', wordDict=[] -> false
